section: Growth of nationalism - factors; pre-Congress political associations
subsections: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association

accepted.s: Which was the first political association in India?
accepted.x: The Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha, established in 1836 by associates of Raja Rammohan Roy, is regarded as the first political association in India.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the earliest organisation in a sequence.

accepted.s: The Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha was established in
accepted.x: The Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha was established in 1836.
accepted.tq: Use the year-based elimination among closely spaced dates.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Landholders' Society was established in 1838.
2. It represented zamindar interests.
3. Dwarkanath Tagore, Prasanna Kumar Tagore and Radhakant Deb were associated with its foundation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Landholders' Society was founded in 1838 to represent zamindar interests, with Dwarkanath Tagore, Prasanna Kumar Tagore and Radhakant Deb among its founders.
accepted.tq: Check the organisation, its purpose and its associated founders separately.

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the Bengal British India Society established on 20 April 1843?
accepted.x: George Thomson founded the Bengal British India Society along with Dwarkanath Tagore, Chandra Mohan Chatterjee and Parmananda Maitra.
accepted.tq: Identify the founder from a closely related list of association leaders.

accepted.s: The Bengal British India Society primarily aimed at
o: Demanding immediate independence from British rule
Welfare of all classes while remaining loyal to the Crown
Promoting the interests of zamindars alone
accepted.x: The Bengal British India Society worked for the welfare of all classes and professed loyalty to the British Crown.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated objective from the objectives of neighbouring associations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the British Indian Association?
o: It was established in 1851 through the merger of two earlier associations.
It was established in 1866 in London by Dadabhai Naoroji.
It was established in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee alone.
It was established in 1885 by Pherozeshah Mehta.
accepted.x: The British Indian Association was formed in 1851 through the merger of the Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society.
accepted.tq: Use the merger detail to separate organisations with similar constitutional objectives.

accepted.s: Who was the first president of the British Indian Association?
accepted.x: Radhakant Deb was the first president of the British Indian Association, while Debendranath Tagore served as its secretary.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the president and secretary of the same organisation.

accepted.s: The Madras Native Association began as an adjunct of the
accepted.x: The Madras Native Association initially functioned as an adjunct of the British Indian Association before becoming independent.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional relationship between two similarly named associations.

accepted.s: The Bombay Association, established in 1852, was founded by
accepted.x: Jagannath Shankarseth founded the Bombay Association in 1852, the first organised political body in Bombay.
accepted.tq: Match the association with its founder and location.

accepted.s: Who founded the East India Association?
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in 1866 to influence British public opinion.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of founder and purpose.

accepted.s: The first president of the East India Association was
accepted.x: Lord Lyveden was the first president of the East India Association.
accepted.tq: Separate the founder from the first president.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following associations in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
B. East India Association
C. India League
D. Indian Association
accepted.x: The correct order is East India Association (1866), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870), India League (1875), and Indian Association (1876).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest organisations first, then arrange the middle dates.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha is correct?
o: It was established on 2 April 1870 by M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi.
It was established in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose.
It was established in 1885 by Pherozeshah Mehta and K.T. Telang.
It was established in 1875 by Sisir Kumar Ghosh for political education.
accepted.x: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was established on 2 April 1870 by M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi; S.H. Chiplunkar is also associated with it in some accounts.
accepted.tq: Test the exact date and founders against nearby pre-Congress bodies.

accepted.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha served primarily as a
o: Bridge between the government and the people
Literary association devoted to Bengali studies
accepted.x: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha acted as a bridge between the government and the people and also nurtured Tilak's political development.
accepted.tq: Infer the organisation from its distinctive institutional role.

accepted.s: The India League was founded in 1875 by
accepted.x: Sisir Kumar Ghosh founded the India League in 1875 for the political education of the masses.
accepted.tq: Direct founder-year recall.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the East India Association?
o: To influence British opinion regarding India
To organise agricultural banks in Andhra
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji established the East India Association in London in 1866 to influence British opinion on Indian affairs.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its distinctive objective.

accepted.s: The Bombay Presidency Association was established in 1885 by
o: Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose
accepted.x: Pherozeshah Mehta and K.T. Telang established the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885 to promote political thinking among western Indian youth.
accepted.tq: Use the founder pair to distinguish presidency-level associations.

accepted.s: The Madras Native Association was founded on 26 February 1852 by
accepted.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association and served as its first president.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the founder and exact date.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the secretary of the Madras Native Association?
accepted.x: Somasundaram Chettiyar served as the secretary of the Madras Native Association.
accepted.tq: Separate the president-founder from the secretary of the same body.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty had started which newspaper in 1844?
accepted.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty started the newspaper Crescent in 1844.
accepted.tq: Match the individual with the associated publication.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the activities of the Madras Native Association?
o: Beginning as an adjunct of the British Indian Association
Demanding the establishment of agricultural banks in Angalur in 1900
accepted.x: Agricultural banks at Angalur were associated with a Krishna District Association conference in 1900, not the Madras Native Association.
accepted.tq: Find the activity belonging to a different Madras-area association.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Moturpha was a tax imposed on
accepted.x: Moturpha referred to a tax on trades and occupations. One fragment also describes it specifically as a tax on looms.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an occupational tax from land and trade duties.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was established on 16 May 1884. Who was its president?
accepted.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu was the president of the Madras Mahajana Sabha, while P. Anandacharlu was its secretary.
accepted.tq: Test the office-holder against other founders of the same association.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Madras Mahajana Sabha is correct?
o: It demanded larger legislative councils and greater Indian representation.
It was founded in 1892 as the first district association in Madras Presidency.
It was established in London to influence British opinion.
accepted.x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha demanded larger councils and greater Indian representation. The other descriptions refer to different associations.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional demand associated with the correct organisation.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Kakinada Literary Association submitted memorandums during 1884–85 demanding
o: A lower ICS age limit and separate examinations for Indians
The abolition of the Madras Mahajana Sabha
The introduction of jury trials for Europeans only
A higher ICS age limit and simultaneous examinations
accepted.x: The Kakinada Literary Association demanded that the ICS age limit be raised and that the examinations be held simultaneously.
accepted.tq: Link a specific association with its distinctive constitutional demand.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Krishna District Association, founded in 1892, was established by
accepted.x: Ramaswamy Gupta founded the Krishna District Association in 1892, the first district association in the Madras Presidency.
accepted.tq: Direct founder recall for a regional association.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the conferences of the Krishna District Association?
accepted.x: The conferences were held at Guntur in 1892, Machilipatnam in 1893, Eluru in 1894 and Angalur in 1900.
accepted.tq: Arrange the venues using the years attached to each conference.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Angalur — demand for simultaneous ICS examinations
accepted.x: Angalur was associated with agricultural banks in 1900. The demand for simultaneous ICS examinations was associated with the Kakinada Literary Association.
accepted.tq: Locate the activity wrongly transferred from one association to another.
accepted.sec: Madras associations - Madras Native Association, Madras Mahajana Sabha, Krishna District Association  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal objective of the Ilbert Bill was to allow
o: Indian members to vote in British parliamentary elections
Indians to hold the office of Viceroy
Indian judges and magistrates to try Europeans in criminal cases
European judges to try only Indian civil servants
accepted.x: The Ilbert Bill sought to empower Indian judges and magistrates to try Europeans in criminal cases.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal power involved rather than the political context alone.

accepted.s: The violent European opposition to the Ilbert Bill came to be known as the
accepted.x: The violent protest by Europeans against the Ilbert Bill was popularly described as the White Mutiny.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive label attached to the controversy.

accepted.s: Which compromise was introduced when the Ilbert Bill was watered down in 1884?
o: Only European judges could hear criminal cases involving Indians.
A European accused could claim a jury consisting of at least half Europeans.
Indian judges were prohibited from hearing civil cases.
The Bill was extended to all princely states without qualification.
accepted.x: The compromise allowed a European accused to claim a jury with at least half its members being Europeans.
accepted.tq: Test the precise compromise provision rather than the broad controversy.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ilbert Bill controversy:
1. It exposed the racial attitude of the British in India.
2. It demonstrated to Indians the effectiveness of organised agitation.
3. The Indian Association supported the Bill against European agitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The controversy revealed British racism, encouraged organised Indian political action and saw the Indian Association support the Bill.
accepted.tq: Combine the consequences and the role of the Indian Association.

accepted.s: Who wrote Anandamath, published in 1882?
accepted.x: Anandamath was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in 1882 and was set against the background of the Sannyasi Rebellion.
accepted.tq: Match the nationalist work with its author and year.

accepted.s: Anandamath is set in the background of the
accepted.x: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's Anandamath is set in the context of the Sannyasi Rebellion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the literary setting from other nineteenth-century uprisings.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Vande Mataram is correct?
o: It appeared in Anandamath and was first sung at the Indian National Congress by Rabindranath Tagore in 1896 at Calcutta.
It appeared in Nil Darpan and was first sung at the Congress in 1885 at Bombay.
It was written for the Krishna Patrika in 1905 by Dinabandhu Mitra.
It was first sung at the Congress in 1883 by Surendranath Banerjee.
accepted.x: Vande Mataram appeared in Anandamath and was first sung at the Indian National Congress by Rabindranath Tagore in Calcutta in 1896. It later became a nationalist war cry.
accepted.tq: Check the work, performer, venue and year together.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novels as described in relation to his works?
o: Durgeshnandini — first novel; Anandamath — 1882; Rajasimha, Rajani and Indira — other novels
Anandamath — first novel; Durgeshnandini — 1882; Rajani — nationalist poem
Rajasimha — first novel; Indira — 1882; Durgeshnandini — historical poem
Rajani — first novel; Anandamath — 1860; Indira — political association
accepted.x: Durgeshnandini was Bankim's first novel. His other novels listed here include Rajasimha, Rajani and Indira, while Anandamath was published in 1882.
accepted.tq: Separate the author's first novel from his other works and publication year.

accepted.s: Who wrote Nil Darpan, published in 1860?
accepted.x: Dinabandhu Mitra wrote Nil Darpan, which was published in 1860.
accepted.tq: Direct author-year recall for nationalist literature.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the nationalist poets of Bengal?
accepted.x: Rangalal Banerjee, Hem Chandra Banerjee and Nabin Chandra Sen were listed as nationalist poets of Bengal. Y. Doraiswamayya was associated with the Telugu translation of Vande Mataram.
accepted.tq: Find the person belonging to the translation detail rather than the Bengali poets' group.

accepted.s: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by
o: P. Anandacharlu and G. Subramania Iyer
Rangalal Banerjee and Hem Chandra Banerjee
Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose
accepted.x: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by Y. Doraiswamayya and M. Ramarao.
accepted.tq: Match the translation with its translators.

accepted.s: The first nationalist song in Andhra, titled 'The Cry of Mother India', appeared in
accepted.x: 'The Cry of Mother India' appeared in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905 and was regarded as the first nationalist song in Andhra.
accepted.tq: Combine the title, publication and exact date to identify the correct option.
